title: Whole Counsel of God
definition: The whole counsel of God refers to the full breadth of biblical truth God has revealed, not merely favorite passages or comfortable themes.
summary: Faithful ministry teaches Scripture widely and deeply so God's people are formed by the fullness of His Word.
christFocus: The whole counsel of God centers on Christ and includes the Gospel, doctrine, repentance, holiness, hope, warning, comfort, and mission.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Whole Counsel of God teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to whole counsel of god by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
